title: C - exercise book
text:
C - exercise book
Here you will find a collection of programming exercises in the C language. The inspiration was to compile tasks created during teaching classes carried out at the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science of the University of Warmia and Mazury in Olsztyn.
Some of the exercises have been machine-translated into English. In case of any ambiguities, please get in touch via email.




Krzaczkowski, Jacek. 2011. Zadania z Programowania w Języku c/c++, Cz. I. Instytut Informatyki UMCS Lublin.

title: 1  Input and Output Operations
text:
Write a programme that asks the user to enter a single integer, then displays it on the screen.
Create a programme that reads two floating-point numbers from the user and prints their difference.
Design an application that asks the user for their year of birth, then prints the previous year (one less).
Write a programme that reads three integers from the user and prints their average as a floating-point value.
Create a programme that asks the user to enter two letters (characters), then prints them in reverse order.
Write a programme that asks the user to enter a single floating-point number, then doubles its value and prints the result.
Create a programme that reads a floating-point number from the user representing an amount in dollars, then prints how much that is in euros, using a fixed exchange rate (e.g. 1 dollar = 0.85 euros).
Write a programme that displays the following text on the screen: This is a quote: "I often use the C language.". Ensure that the quotation marks are correctly displayed as part of the string.
Create a programme that prints a Windows folder path to standard output, e.g. C:\Program Files\MyApplication\ (hardcoded, without retrieving anything from the system) or C:\\Program Files\\MyApplication\\.
Design a programme that demonstrates how to print the following text on the screen: Special characters: \t (tab), \n (newline), % (percent), \\ (backslash).
Write a programme that reads two rational numbers from standard input representing the lengths of the legs of a right-angled triangle. Then calculate and display the length of the hypotenuse.
Write a programme that reads an integer from standard input and prints its absolute value to standard output.
Write a programme that reads a floating-point number from standard input and prints its absolute value to standard output.
Find an example and display on standard output a case where the addition of floating-point numbers is not associative.

title: 2  Arithmetic Operators
text:
Write a programme that calculates the remainder of dividing the sum of two integers by a third integer.
Create a programme that calculates the difference of squares of two given integers.
Write a programme that calculates the product of the difference of two integers and a third integer.
Design a programme that calculates the geometric mean of the absolute values of three given integers.
Write a programme that calculates the square of the sum of two given integers.
Create a programme that calculates the sum of squares of three given integers.
Write a programme that calculates how many times one given integer fits into another given integer.
Design a programme that calculates the square of the difference of two given integers.
Write a programme that calculates the quotient of the sum of two integers divided by their difference.
Create a programme that calculates the sum of three consecutive integers, starting from a given integer.
Find the arithmetic mean of three floating-point numbers.
Calculate the value of the expression \(\frac{1}{\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c}}\), where \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) are non-zero.
Calculate the value of \(e^x\) for small values of \(x\), e.g. \(|x| < 0.01\), approximating \(e^x\) as \(1 + x\), without using exponential functions.
Calculate the area of a triangle with sides \(a\), \(b\) and the angle \(C\) between them in degrees, using the formula \(0.5 \cdot a \cdot b \cdot \sin C\), assuming \(\sin C \approx C\) for small angles in radians.
Calculate \(\sqrt[3]{x}\) for small values of \(x\), e.g. \(|x| < 0.01\), approximating \(\sqrt[3]{x} \approx 1 + \frac{1}{3}x\), without using any root functions.

title: 3  Conditional statements, conditional operator
text:
In the following exercises, use if, if else, or switch case as the conditional statement. The conditional operator refers to ?.

Write a programme that asks the user to enter an integer. The programme should display whether the entered number is positive, negative, or equal to zero.
Write a programme that takes two integers from the user and displays the larger of the two.
Write a programme that asks the user to enter a grade on a scale from 1 to 5. The programme should display a description of the grade: fail (1), poor (2), satisfactory (3), good (4), very good (5). For a number outside the range, the programme should display an error message.
Write a programme that asks the user to enter three distinct integers and displays the smallest of them.
Write a programme that asks the user for a year and checks whether the given year is a leap year. A leap year is one that is divisible by 4 but not divisible by 100, unless it is also divisible by 400.
Write a programme that takes two integers from the user and displays whether the sum of both numbers is even or odd.
Write a programme that takes three floating-point numbers a, b, c from the user. Treat them as the coefficients of a quadratic equation \(ax^2+bx+c=0\). Print all solution variants of this equation to standard output.
Write a programme that takes two integers as input from the user and uses the conditional operator to find and display the larger of the two.
Write a programme that takes three integers as input from the user and uses the conditional operator to find and display the smallest of them.
Using the conditional operator ?, write a programme that takes a single integer from the user and displays “even” or “odd” depending on the value of the number.
Create a programme that asks the user to enter two floating-point numbers and uses the conditional operator to display which of them is larger, or whether they are equal to two decimal places.
Using the conditional operator, write a programme that asks the user to enter a grade on a scale from 0 to 100 and displays “Pass” if the grade is greater than or equal to 51, or “Fail” otherwise.
Write a programme that takes a year as input from the user and uses the conditional operator to check whether it is a leap year. The programme should display “Leap year” or “Not a leap year” depending on the result.

title: 4  Bitwise operators
text:
Swap the values of two integer variables without using an additional variable.
Check whether an integer is even or odd using bitwise operators.
Determine the value of the bit at a specified position in an integer.
Clear the value of the bit at a specified position in an integer.
Invert the values of all bits in an integer.
Shift the bits of an integer a specified number of positions to the left.
Shift the bits of an integer a specified number of positions to the right.
Determine the XOR of two integers.

title: 5  Debugging - basics
text:
Below is code written in C. Some lines contain comments. Your task is to fill in the values of the corresponding variables after each line of code is executed. Adding new lines or disrupting the code structure means the task was done incorrectly.

#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int a = 10; // a = , b =
    int b = 5;  // a = , b =
    a = a + b;  // a = , b =
    b = a - b;  // a = , b =
    a = a - b;  // a = , b =
    b = a * b;  // a = , b =
    a = b / a;  // a = , b =
    b = a << 2; // a = , b =
    a = b >> 1; // a = , b =
    b = a & b;  // a = , b =
    a = a ^ b;  // a = , b =
    b = ~a;     // a = , b =
    return 0;
}

Below is code written in C. Some lines contain comments. Your task is to fill in the values of the corresponding variables after each line of code is executed. Adding new lines or disrupting the code structure means the task was done incorrectly.

#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int a = 10; // a = , b = , c =
    int b = 5;  // a = , b = , c =
    int c = 0;  // a = , b = , c =
    a = a + b;  // a = , b = , c =
    b = a - b;  // a = , b = , c =
    a = a - b;  // a = , b = , c =
    c = a;      // a = , b = , c =
    a = b * c;  // a = , b = , c =
    b = a / c;  // a = , b = , c =
    c = b << 2; // a = , b = , c =
    b = c >> 1; // a = , b = , c =
    a = b & c;  // a = , b = , c =
    c = a ^ b;  // a = , b = , c =
    b = ~c;     // a = , b = , c =
    return 0;
}

Below is code written in C. Some lines contain comments. Your task is to fill in the values of the corresponding variables after each line of code is executed. Adding new lines or disrupting the code structure means the task was done incorrectly.

#include <stdio.h>
int main() {
    int x = 7;    // x = , y = , z = 
    int y = 3;    // x = , y = , z = 
    int z = 12;   // x = , y = , z = 
    x = x * 2;    // x = , y = , z = 
    y = y + x;    // x = , y = , z = 
    z = z - y;    // x = , y = , z = 
    x = z / 2;    // x = , y = , z = 
    y = x % 3;    // x = , y = , z = 
    z = x + y;    // x = , y = , z = 
    x = z++;      // x = , y = , z = 
    y = ++x;      // x = , y = , z = 
    z = y--;      // x = , y = , z = 
    return 0;
}

Below is code written in C. Some lines contain comments. Your task is to fill in the values of the corresponding variables after each line of code is executed. Adding new lines or disrupting the code structure means the task was done incorrectly.

#include <stdio.h>
int main() {
    int p = 15;   // p = , q = , r = 
    int q = 6;    // p = , q = , r = 
    int r = 1;    // p = , q = , r = 
    p = p | q;    // p = , q = , r = 
    q = p & 10;   // p = , q = , r = 
    r = r << 3;   // p = , q = , r = 
    p = p ^ r;    // p = , q = , r = 
    q = q >> 1;   // p = , q = , r = 
    r = ~p;       // p = , q = , r = 
    p = q | r;    // p = , q = , r = 
    q = p & r;    // p = , q = , r = 
    r = r ^ q;    // p = , q = , r = 
    return 0;
}

Below is code written in C. Some lines contain comments. Your task is to fill in the values of the corresponding variables after each line of code is executed. Adding new lines or disrupting the code structure means the task was done incorrectly.

#include <stdio.h>
int main() {
    float a = 10.5;  // a = , b = , c = 
    float b = 2.0;   // a = , b = , c = 
    float c = 0.5;   // a = , b = , c = 
    a = a / b;       // a = , b = , c = 
    b = b * 3;       // a = , b = , c = 
    c = a + b;       // a = , b = , c = 
    a = c - a;       // a = , b = , c = 
    b = b / 2;       // a = , b = , c = 
    c = a * b;       // a = , b = , c = 
    a = c + 0.5;     // a = , b = , c = 
    b = a - c;       // a = , b = , c = 
    c = a / b;       // a = , b = , c = 
    return 0;
}

Below is code written in C. Some lines contain comments. Your task is to fill in the values of the corresponding variables after each line of code is executed. Adding new lines or disrupting the code structure means the task was done incorrectly.

#include <stdio.h>
int main() {
    int m = 20;   // m = , n = , k = 
    int n = 4;    // m = , n = , k = 
    int k = 2;    // m = , n = , k = 
    m += n;       // m = , n = , k = 
    n -= k;       // m = , n = , k = 
    k *= 3;       // m = , n = , k = 
    m /= 2;       // m = , n = , k = 
    n += m;       // m = , n = , k = 
    k %= n;       // m = , n = , k = 
    m <<= 1;      // m = , n = , k = 
    n >>= 2;      // m = , n = , k = 
    k ^= m;       // m = , n = , k = 
    return 0;
}

title: 6  Loops
text:
The tasks should be solved without arrays, strings, pointers, or built-in math functions. Do not create your own functions either.

Write a program that displays all integers from 1 to 100 using a for loop.
Create a program that asks the user to enter an integer n, and then displays the sum of all integers from 1 to n using a while loop.
Write a program that reads integers from the user until zero is entered, and then displays the sum of all positive numbers and the sum of all negative numbers, using a do-while loop.
Create a program that calculates and displays the factorial of a non-negative integer entered by the user, using a for loop.
Write a program that displays the first 10 numbers of the Fibonacci sequence using a while loop.
Write a program that asks the user to enter a positive integer n, and then calculates and displays \(\lfloor \sqrt{n} \rfloor\) (the integer part/floor of the square root).
Write a program that asks the user to enter a positive integer n, and then calculates and displays \(\lceil \sqrt{n} \rceil\) (the ceiling of the square root).
Write a program that asks the user to enter 10 positive integers and arranges them into a sequence \(a_1, \ldots, a_{10}\). Calculate and display how many elements of the sequence satisfy the inequality \(a_k < \frac{a_{k-1}+a_{k+1}}{2}\) for \(1<k<10\).
Write a program that asks the user to enter a positive integer \(n\), and then \(n\) positive integers and arranges them into a sequence \(a_1, \ldots, a_n\). Calculate and display how many elements of the sequence satisfy the inequality \(a_k < \frac{a_{k-1}+a_{k+1}}{2}\) for \(1<k<n\).
Write a program that checks the divisibility of a number n by all numbers from 2 to n/2. The program should print all divisors of that number. Read the value of n from the user.
Write a program that reads an integer n and prints all its digits from the end (starting from the units digit) and calculates their sum.
Write a program implementing the Euclidean algorithm in an iterative version using subtraction. The program should read two natural numbers a and b, and then print their greatest common divisor.
Write a program implementing the Euclidean algorithm in an iterative version using division. The program should read two natural numbers a and b, and then print their greatest common divisor.
Write a program that checks whether a given number n is a prime number. The program should check all potential divisors from 2 to the square root of n (use a loop to calculate the square root). Print an appropriate message.
Write a program simulating change-making. The program should read the amount to be given as change and print how many coins of denominations 5, 2, and 1 should be used to minimize the total number of coins. Print the number of coins of each type.
Write a program that determines the approximate value of the square root of a number a using Newton’s method (iterative). The initial approximation is x₀ = a/2, and subsequent values are calculated using the formula x_{i+1} = (x_i + a/x_i)/2. Perform 10 iterations of the algorithm and print the final result.
Write a program that reads from the user the degree of a polynomial, the coefficients (from the highest power to the constant term), and the value of x. Calculate the value of the polynomial using Horner’s method, utilizing a loop. Display the result of the calculations.

title: 7  Functions
text:
Solve the exercises without using arrays, strings, pointers, or built-in math functions. You may create additional helper functions for each exercise. For each function described in the exercise, provide a test case (call it at least once with a valid argument). The exercises use the camelCase naming convention. Pay attention to whether the function should return a value or print it.

Write a function sumTwoNumbers that takes two integers as arguments. The function should print the sum of the numbers passed as arguments. Create a test case.
Write a function calculateAbsoluteValue that takes a floating-point number as an argument. The function should return the absolute value of the number passed as an argument. Create a test case.
Write a function calculateFactorial that takes a non-negative integer as an argument. The function should return the factorial of the number passed as an argument, computed using a non-recursive method. Create a test case.
Write a function sumNumbers that takes a positive integer \(n\) as an argument. The function should return the sum of numbers from 1 to \(n\) inclusive. Create a test case.
Write a function sumSquares that takes a positive integer \(n\) as an argument. The function should return the sum of squares of numbers from 1 to \(n\) inclusive. Create a test case.
Write a function calculatePowerOfTwo that takes an integer \(n\) as an argument. The function should return the value of \(2^n\). Create a test case.
Write a function calculateSquareRootFloor that takes a non-negative integer \(n\) as an argument. The function should return the integer part of the square root of \(n\). Create a test case.
Write a function countFunctionCalls that takes no arguments. The function should count and print to standard output the number of times it has been called since the program started. Create a test case. Use static variables.
Write a function calculateFactorialRecursively that takes a non-negative integer \(n\) as an argument. The function should return the factorial of \(n\), computed using a recursive method. Create a test case.
Write a function calculateFibonacciRecursively that takes a non-negative integer \(n\) as an argument. The function should return the \(n\)-th term of the Fibonacci sequence, computed using a recursive method. Create a test case.
Write a function calculateArithmeticSequenceRecursively that takes two positive integers as arguments: \(n\) (the index of the sequence term to compute) and \(d\) (the common difference of the arithmetic sequence), assuming the initial term \(a_1\) equals 1. The function should return the \(n\)-th term of the arithmetic sequence, computed using a recursive method. Create a test case.
Write a function calculateGeometricSequenceRecursively that takes two positive integers as arguments: \(n\) (the index of the sequence term to compute) and \(d\) (the common ratio of the geometric sequence), assuming the initial term \(a_1\) equals 1. The function should return the \(n\)-th term of the geometric sequence, computed using a recursive method. Create a test case.
Write a function calculate13 that takes a positive integer \(n\) as an argument. The function should return the value defined by \(f(n) = 2f(n-1) + 3\), where \(f(1) = 1\). Create a test case.
Write a function calculate14 that takes a positive integer \(n\) as an argument. The function should return the value defined by \(f(n) = 3f(n-1) - 1\), where \(f(1) = 2\). Create a test case.
Write a function calculate15 that takes a positive integer \(n\) as an argument. The function should return the value defined by \(f(n) = f(n-1) + 2f(n-2)\), where \(f(1) = 1\) and \(f(2) = 2\). Create a test case.
Write a function calculate16 that takes a positive integer \(n\) as an argument. The function should return the value defined by \(f(n) = 2f(n-1) + 3f(n-2)\), where \(f(1) = 2\) and \(f(2) = 3\). Create a test case.
Write a recursive function calculate17 that takes a non-negative integer \(n\) as an argument. The function should return the value defined by \(f(n) = f(0)+f(1)+\ldots +f(n-1)\), where \(f(0) = f(1) = 1\). Create a test case.
Write a recursive function calculateGCD that takes two positive integers \(n\) and \(m\) as arguments. The function should return the greatest common divisor (GCD) of these numbers using the Euclidean algorithm. Create a test case.

title: 8  Pointers
text:
The exercises should be solved without interpreting pointers as arrays.

Copy or retype the code and check the output on standard output:

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main()
{
    printf("%zu\n", sizeof(int));
    printf("%zu\n", sizeof(int*));
    return 0;
}

In a single file, perform the following tasks:


Write a function sum with two arguments of type int. The function should return the sum of the values passed through the arguments. Create a test case.
Write a function sumVals with two arguments that are pointers to variables of type int. The function should return the sum of the values pointed to by these arguments. Create a test case.
Write a function addPtr with three arguments that are pointers to variables of type int. The function should be a procedure (return type void). The function should set the value of the variable pointed to by the third argument to the sum of the values pointed to by the first two arguments. Create a test case.


Write a function copyInt with the arguments: x of type int and w, which is a pointer to int. The function should copy the value of x to the variable pointed to by w. Create a test case.
Write a function findMax with two arguments: a pointer num1 to a constant value of type double and a constant pointer num2 to a variable of type double. The function should return the greater value among those pointed to by num1 and num2. Create a test case.
Write a function initInts that takes no arguments and allocates a block of three variables of type int, setting their values to 5, -12, 33 respectively. The function returns a pointer to the middle variable. Create a test case in the main function that displays the values from the block created by the function.
Write a function initFloats that takes no arguments and allocates a block of three variables of type float, setting their values to 4.5, 2.3, -4.2 respectively. The function returns a pointer to the first variable in the block. Create a test case in the main function that displays the values from the block created by the function.
Write a function initFlts that takes no arguments and allocates a block of four variables of type float, setting their values to 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, and 3.5 respectively. The function returns a pointer to the last variable in the block. Create a test case in main to display the values from the block created by the function.
Write a function sumToPtr with three arguments: two pointers to constants of type int and a pointer to a variable of type int. The function should store the sum of the constant values pointed to by the first and second arguments into the variable pointed to by the third argument. Create a test case.
Write a function sqrCopy with two arguments: a pointer to a constant of type int and a pointer to a variable of type int. The function should copy the square of the constant’s value to the variable pointed to by the second argument. Create a test case.
Write a function subPtrs with two arguments: a pointer num1 to a constant value of type double and a constant pointer num2 to a variable of type double. The function should return the difference of the values pointed to by num1 and num2. Create a test case.
Write a function sumSqrs with two arguments: a pointer num1 to a constant value of type int and a constant pointer num2 to a variable of type int. The function should return the sum of the squares of the values pointed to by num1 and num2. Create a test case.
Write a function linFuncVal with three arguments: a pointer a to a constant value of type float, a constant pointer b to a variable of type float, and a pointer x to a constant value of type float. The function should compute and return the value of the linear function y=ax+b for argument x, where a and b are pointed to by the corresponding pointers. Create a test case.
Write a function minPtr with three arguments that are pointers to variables of type int. The function returns a pointer to the variable with the smallest value among those pointed to by the arguments. Create a test case in main to display the smallest value among three variables.
Write a function multPtrs with two arguments: a pointer num1 to a constant value of type double and a constant pointer num2 to a variable of type double. The function returns the product of the values pointed to by these pointers. Create a test case.
Write a function absVal with one argument, which is a pointer to a variable of type int. The function computes the absolute value of the variable pointed to by the pointer and updates that variable. Create a test case in main to display the value of the updated variable.
Write a function swap with two arguments: a pointer ptr1 to a variable of type int and a pointer ptr2 to another variable of the same type. The function swaps the values pointed to by the pointers. Create a test case.
Write a function swapSign with two arguments: a pointer ptr1 to a variable of type double and a pointer ptr2 to another variable of the same type. The function swaps the values pointed to by the pointers if they have different signs. Otherwise, it does nothing. Create a test case.
Write a function swapIfGreater that has two arguments. The first argument is a pointer ptr1 to a variable of type int, and the second argument is a pointer ptr2 to a variable of type int. The function should swap the values pointed to by these pointers, but only if the value pointed to by the first pointer is greater than the value pointed to by the second pointer. The function does not return any value. Create a test case for the function.
Write a function swapMaxMiddle that takes three pointers to variables of type int as arguments. The function should swap the values of the largest and the middle (in terms of value in non-decreasing order) variables pointed to by the pointers. Create a test case in main to display the values of the variables before and after the swap on the console.
Write a function swapFirstPositive that takes three pointers to variables of type int as arguments. The function should swap the values of the first and the first positive variable among those pointed to by the pointers. If there is no positive variable, the function should not make any changes. Create a test case in main to display the values of the variables before and after the swap on the console.
Write a function swapOddEven that takes four pointers to variables of type int as arguments. The function should swap the values of the variables so that all even values are at the beginning and odd values are at the end (the order within groups does not matter). Create a test case in main to display the values of the variables before and after the swap on the console.
Write a function modifyThroughPtr with two arguments: a pointer to a variable of type int and a value of type int. The function should perform the following operations: if the second value is positive — increase the value of the variable pointed to by the first argument by that value; if the second value is negative — decrease the value of the first variable by the absolute value of the second argument; and if the second value is 0 — do not change the value. The function returns the address of the modified variable. Create a test case.

title: 9  Function Pointers
text:
Write a function calculate that takes two arguments: a pointer to a function operation and an integer number. The function operation should take one argument of type int and return a value of type int. The function calculate should call the function operation with the argument number and return its result. Create a test case.
Write a function called applyFunction that takes three arguments: a pointer to a function func that takes one argument of type int and returns int, and two integers: start and end. The function applyFunction should call the function func for each number in the range from start to end (inclusive) and print the results to standard output. Create a test case.
Write a function that takes three arguments:


two pointers to functions with one argument of type int returning a value of type int,
a positive value n of type int,

and returns 1 if the functions received as arguments have the same sign for integer values from 0 to \(n\), and returns 0 otherwise. Create a test case.

Write a function calculateOperation that takes as arguments: a pointer to a function operation that takes two arguments of type double and returns double, and two arguments of type double — number1 and number2. The function calculateOperation should return the result of calling the function operation on the arguments number1 and number2. Create a test case.
Write a function modifyAndSum that takes as an argument a pointer to a function modifier that takes one argument of type int and returns int, and two arguments of type int: number1 and number2. The function modifyAndSum should modify both numbers using the function modifier and return their sum. An example of a modifier function could be a function that increments a number by 1 or changes the sign of a number. Create a test case.
Create a function applyCondition that takes three arguments: a pointer to a function condition returning a value of type int and taking an int, a pointer to a function action also taking and returning int, and an integer value value. The function applyCondition should first call condition with value as the argument. If the result is 1, applyCondition should then call action on value and return the result. Otherwise, it should return value unchanged. Create a test case.
Create a function executeSequence that takes two arguments: a pointer to a function operation returning void and taking an int, and an integer count. The function executeSequence should call the function operation exactly count times, passing consecutive numbers from 1 to count as the argument. Create a test case.
Create a function modifyValue that takes an argument of type int and a pointer to a function modifier that takes no arguments but returns a value of type int. The function modifyValue should add the result of calling the function modifier to the passed value and return the resulting sum. Create a test case.
Create a function processPair that takes two integers and a pointer to a function processor that returns double and takes two arguments of type int. The function processPair should call processor with the passed numbers, round the result down to the nearest integer, and return that value as int. Create a test case.
Create a function transformLoop that takes a pointer to a function transform returning int and taking int, an initial value start, and a number of iterations iterations. The function should perform the specified number of iterations, in each iteration assigning to the result variable the value returned by the function transform called on the result from the previous iteration (on the value start in the first iteration). At the end, the function should return the final value. Create a test case.
Create a function computeWithFallback that takes three arguments: a pointer to a function primary taking two parameters of type int and returning int, a pointer to a function backup with the same signature, and two integer values a and b. The function computeWithFallback should call the function primary with the arguments a and b. If the result of the function primary is less than zero, the function computeWithFallback should call backup with the same arguments a and b and return the result of that function. Otherwise (when the result of the function primary is greater than or equal to zero), the function computeWithFallback should return the result of the function primary. The function computeWithFallback should return a value of type int. Create a test case.

title: 10  One-Dimensional Arrays
text:
The exercises should be solved without converting numbers to strings. In the exercises, do not use double pointers or equivalents of multi-dimensional arrays — the syntax should use a single dimension only. In the exercises, do not consider an array of size zero, as size-related arguments are positive.

Write a function findMaxValue that takes as arguments an integer array numbers and its size size (a positive integer). The function should search the array and display the maximum value found in it. Create a test case.
Write a function average whose arguments are a positive integer \(n\) and an \(n\)-element array tab of elements of type int, and returns the arithmetic mean as a floating-point number. Create a test case.
Write a function sumSquares whose arguments are a positive integer \(n\) and an \(n\)-element array tab of elements of type int, and returns the sum of squares of the array elements. Create a test case.
Write a function copyArr that takes three arguments: a positive integer n and two n-element arrays tab1, tab2 of elements of type int, and copies the elements of array tab1 to array tab2 in order. Create a test case.
Write a function revCopy that takes three arguments: a positive integer n and two n-element arrays tab1, tab2 of elements of type int, and copies the elements of array tab1 to array tab2 in reverse order. Create a test case.
Write a function reverseArr whose arguments are a positive integer n representing the array size and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should reverse the order of elements in the array tab directly in place, without using an additional array to store results. Create a test case.
Write a function maxValue whose arguments are a positive integer n representing the array size and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should search the array and return the largest value found in it. Assume the array is not empty. Create a test case.
Write a function minValue whose arguments are a positive integer n representing the array size and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should search the array and return the smallest value found in it. Assume the array is not empty. Create a test case.
Write a function maxIdx whose arguments are a positive integer n representing the array size and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should find and return the index of the largest element in the array. If more than one element has the maximum value, the function should return the index of the first one (i.e., the smallest possible index). Assume the array is not empty. Create a test case.
Write a function minIdxMax whose arguments are a positive integer n representing the array size and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should search the array and return the index of the smallest element in the array. If there are multiple identical smallest elements, return the largest possible index among them. Assume the array is not empty. Create a test case.
Write a function shiftLeft whose arguments are a positive integer n representing the array size and an n-element array tab of elements of type float. The function should shift all elements of the array one position to the left, and the last element in the array should be replaced by the first element of the original array. Assume the array is not empty. Create a test case.
Write a function shiftRight2 whose arguments are a positive integer n representing the array size and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should shift all elements of the array two positions to the right. Elements that “fall off” the end of the array should appear at its beginning in the same order. Create a test case.
Write a function shiftLeft whose arguments are a positive integer n representing the array size and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return a pointer to a newly created dynamic array in which all elements have been shifted one position to the left relative to the original array, and the last element of the new array equals the first element of the original array. Create a test case.
Write a function shiftRight whose arguments are a positive integer n representing the array size and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return a pointer to a newly created dynamic array in which all elements have been shifted one position to the right relative to the original array, and the first element of the new array equals the last element of the original array. Create a test case.
Below is code in the C language. Some lines contain comments. Your task is to fill in the values of the corresponding variables after each specific line of code is executed. Adding new lines or disrupting the code structure means incorrect completion of the task.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int foo(int*a,int*b)
{
    return *a-*b;
}

int main()
{
    int tab[] = {3,3,0,0,3,3,-4,-4,0,1};
    int *wsk=tab-1;
    int b = *(wsk+=4); //b=
    int c = b+3; // b=  , c=
    int d = foo(&b,&c); // b=  , c=  , d=
    int e = (wsk+=-1)[4]; // b=  , c=  , d=  , e=
    e = (d *= 2) + (c += 2); // b=  , c=  , d=  , e=
    c = d + (b+=4); // b=  , c=  , d=  , e=
    e= (--c)-(d++);  // b=  , c=  , d=  , e=
    b = *wsk + e; // b=  , c=  , d=  , e=
    return 0;
}

Below is code in the C language. Some lines contain comments. Your task is to fill in the values of the corresponding variables after each specific line of code is executed. Adding new lines or disrupting the code structure means incorrect completion of the task.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int foo(int*a,int*b)
{
    return *a-*b;
}

int main()
{
    int tab[] = {1,5,5,2,3,3,-4,-4,0,1};
    int *wsk=tab-1;
    int b = *(wsk+=4); //b=
    int c = b+3; // b=  , c=
    int d = foo(&b,&c); // b=  , c=  , d=
    int e = (wsk+=-1)[4]; // b=  , c=  , d=  , e=
    e = (d -= 2) - (c += 2); // b=  , c=  , d=  , e=
    c = d + (b+=4); // b=  , c=  , d=  , e=
    e= (--c)-(d++);  // b=  , c=  , d=  , e=
    b = *wsk + e; // b=  , c=  , d=  , e=
    return 0;
}

Write a function called findElement that takes as arguments an integer array, the array size, an integer val to find, and a pointer to a function isEqual. The function isEqual takes two integers as arguments and returns a value of type 0 or 1, indicating whether the numbers are equal, respectively. The function findElement should search the array to find the value val according to the rules defined by the function isEqual, and then return the index of that element in the array (the first one encountered) or -1 if the element does not exist. Create a test case for the function findElement.
Write a function findWithCondition that takes as arguments an integer array, the array size, and a pointer to a function condition. The function condition takes an integer as an argument and returns a value of type 0 or 1, indicating whether the number satisfies a specified condition. The function findWithCondition should search the array to find the last number satisfying the condition defined by the function condition, and then return the index of that element in the array or -1 if no such element exists. Create a test case for the function findWithCondition.
Write a function isSymmetric that takes two arguments: a positive integer \(n\) and an \(n\)-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return the value 1 if the array tab is symmetric (i.e., the first element equals the last, the next equals the second-to-last, etc.) and return zero otherwise. Create a test case for the function.
Write a function areArraysEqual that takes three arguments: a positive integer \(n\) and two \(n\)-element arrays tab1 and tab2 of elements of type int. The function should check whether both arrays are identical. If so, the function should return 1; otherwise, return 0. Create a test case for the function.
Write a function indexOfMaxAbs that takes two arguments: a positive integer \(n\) and an \(n\)-element array tab of elements of type int, and returns the index of the first occurrence of the largest absolute value among the elements stored in array tab. Create a test case for the function.
Write a function rotateLeftByTwo that takes two arguments: a positive integer n (\(n>3\)) and an n-element array tab of elements of type double, and shifts all elements of the array two positions to the left (so that the value of the element at index n-1 ends up at index n-3, the value at index n-2 ends up at index n-4, while the value at index 0 goes to index n-2, and the value at index 1 goes to index n-1). Create a test case for the function.
Write a function multiplyElementwise that takes four arguments: a positive integer n, n-element arrays tab1 and tab2, and an n-element array tab3 of elements of type double. The function should compute the product of the elements of arrays tab1 and tab2 at the same indices and store the results in array tab3. Create a test case for the function.
Write a function sumOddIndices that takes two arguments: a positive integer \(n\) and an \(n\)-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return the sum of the elements located at odd indices. Create a test case.
Write a function countPositiveElements that takes two arguments: a positive integer \(n\) and an \(n\)-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return the number of positive elements in the array. Create a test case.

Example. For an array containing the elements 3,-4,5 the function should return 2.

Write a function doubleOddElements that takes two arguments: a positive integer \(n\) and an \(n\)-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should double the odd-valued elements in the array. Create a test case.
Write a function increaseByIndex that takes two arguments: a positive integer \(n\) and an \(n\)-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should increase the value of each array element by its index. Create a test case.
Write a function multiplyElementwise that takes four arguments: a positive integer n, n-element arrays tab1 and tab2, and an n-element array tab3 of elements of type double. The function should compute the product of the elements of arrays tab1 and tab2 at the same indices and store the results in array tab3. Create a test case for the function.
Write a function sumAboveThreshold that takes three arguments: an integer k, a positive integer n, and an n-element array arr of elements of type int. The function should return the sum of all elements of array arr that are greater than the number k. Create two test cases. Example: for k=10, n=6 and the array 4,12,3,15,8,25 the function should return 52.
Write a function findFirstDivisibleIndex that takes three arguments: a positive integer p, a positive integer n, and an n-element array numbers of elements of type int. The function should return the index of the first occurrence of a number divisible by p in the array numbers. If no element is divisible by p, the function should return -1. Create two test cases. Example: for p=3, n=7 and the array 5,11,9,2,4,7,6 the function should return 2.
Write a function countInRange that takes three arguments: an integer a, an integer b, a positive integer n, and an n-element array data of elements of type int. The function should count how many elements of array data fall within the interval [a,b] (including a and b). Create two test cases. Example: for a=5, b=15, n=8 and the array 3,7,22,10,5,18,9,4 the function should return 4.
Write a function sumDivisibleBy3 that takes two arguments: a positive integer n and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return the sum of elements divisible by 3, and zero if there are no such elements. Create a test case. Example: for the array 7,9,2,6,5 the function should return 15.
Write a function productEven that takes two arguments: a positive integer n and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return the product of even-valued elements, and 1 if there are no such elements. Create a test case. Example: for the array 3,4,5,2,7 the function should return 8.
Write a function countNegInd that takes two arguments: a positive integer n and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return the count of negative elements that are located at even indices of the array. If there are no such elements, the function should return 0. Create a test case. Example: for the array -2,4,-5,-7,6 the function should return 2.
Write a function minArrays that takes four arguments: a positive integer n, n-element arrays tabA, tabB, and tabC of elements of type int. The function should select the minimum value from the elements of arrays tabA and tabB at the same indices and store the results in array tabC. Create a test case. Example: tabA = {7,-2,14}, tabB = {9,6,-3} → tabC = {7,-2,-3}.
Write a function sumArrays that takes four arguments: a positive integer m, m-element arrays array1, array2, and arrayResult of elements of type double. The function should sum the corresponding elements of arrays array1 and array2, and then store the results in array arrayResult. Create a test case.
Write a function sumOdd that takes two arguments: a positive integer n and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return the sum of odd-valued elements, and 0 if there are no such elements. Create a test case. Example: for the array 2,7,4,9,3 the function should return 19.
Write a function multiplyByPosition that takes two arguments: a positive integer n and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function modifies the array by multiplying each element by its index plus 1 (the element at index 0 is multiplied by 1, the element at index 1 by 2, etc.). Create a test case. Example: array {2,3,4} → {2,6,12}.
Write a function decreaseBySquare that takes two arguments: a positive integer n and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should decrease the value of each array element by the square of its index. Create a test case. Example: array {5,10,15,20} → {5,9,11,11}.
Write a function replaceWithPower that takes two arguments: a positive integer n and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should replace the value of each array element with that element raised to the power equal to its index. For index 0, the element remains unchanged. Create a test case. Example: array {2,3,4,-3,-2} → {2,3,16,-27,16}.
Write a function sumOddIndex that takes two arguments: a positive integer n and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return the sum of elements at odd positions, and zero if there are no such elements. Create a test case. Example: for the array 3,-4,5,7,3 the function should return 3, because at odd indices there are -4 and 7.
Write a function countMatching that takes as arguments an integer array, the array size, and a pointer to a function predicate. The function predicate takes an integer as an argument and returns a value of 0 or 1, indicating whether the number satisfies a specified condition. The function countMatching should count and return the number of elements in the array that satisfy the condition. Create a test case. Example: for a function f(x)=1 for even numbers, f(x)=0 for odd numbers, and the array {2,7,8,3,10} the function should return 3.
Write a function productPositive that takes two arguments: a positive integer n and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return the product of all positive elements in the array. If the array contains no positive elements, the function should return 1. Create a test case. Example: for the array {3,-2,5,0,-1,4} the function should return 60.
Write a function countDivisible that takes three arguments: a positive integer n, an n-element array tab of elements of type int, and a positive integer divisor. The function should return the count of array elements that are divisible by divisor. Create a test case. Example: for the array {12,7,-9,15,4,21} and divisor=3 the function should return 4.
Write a function replaceWithFactorial that takes two arguments: a positive integer n and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should replace the value of each array element with the factorial of the absolute value of that element. For values greater than 12, the element should be replaced with the value -1. Create a test case. Example: array {3,-4,0,5,15} → {6,24,1,120,-1}.
Write a function getMaximumValue that takes as arguments a non-empty integer array, the array size, and a pointer to a function isValid. The function isValid takes an integer and returns 0 or 1. The function getMaximumValue should find the largest value among the array elements that satisfy the condition and return it. If no element satisfies the condition, the function should return 0. Create a test case. Example: for f(x)=1 when x%3==0 and the array {7,9,4,12,6} the function should return 12.
Write a function sumOfDivisors that takes two arguments: a positive integer n and an n-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should replace the value of each array element with the sum of all positive divisors of the absolute value of that element (including the number itself). Create a test case. Example: array {6,-12,1,7,-8} → {12,28,1,8,15}.
Write a function sumEvenIndices that takes two arguments: a positive integer \(n\) and an \(n\)-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should return the sum of elements located at even index positions (0, 2, 4, …). Create a test case. Example: for the array {10,3,7,-2,5,8} the function should return 22.
Write a function multiplyByDigitSum that takes two arguments: a positive integer \(n\) and an \(n\)-element array tab of elements of type int. The function should replace the value of each array element with the product of that value and the sum of the digits of the absolute value of that element. Create a test case. Example: array {12,-34,5,100,-7} → {36,-238,25,100,-49}.

title: 11  Strings
text:
Write a function length that takes a string as an argument and returns its length as a value. Use the char type and do not use any built-in functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case.
Write a function countNums that takes a char array as an argument and returns the number of characters in this array that are digits. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for your function.
Write a function countVow that takes a char array as an argument and returns the number of characters in this array that are vowels of the Latin alphabet. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function cmpStrNew that takes two arguments of type char[] (character arrays) and returns 1 if the strings are identical, and 0 otherwise. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function lexComp that takes two arguments of type char[] (character arrays) and returns 1 if the first string comes earlier in lexicographic order than the second one, and 0 otherwise. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function toLowerNew that takes a char array as an argument and converts all uppercase letters in it to lowercase. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function toUpperNew that takes a char array as an argument and converts all lowercase letters in it to uppercase. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function strCopyNew that takes two arguments of type char[] (character arrays): a source and a destination. The function copies the string located in the source array into the destination array. Assume that there is enough space in the destination array. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function strNcopy that takes three arguments: two character arrays nap1, nap2 and a positive integer n. The function copies the first n characters from the string stored in array nap1 to array nap2. If the string in array nap1 is shorter than n characters, the function copies the entire string. The function guarantees that a null-terminating character ('\0') will be placed at the end of the string in array nap2. Assume that there is enough space in array nap2. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function strConcat that takes three character arrays as arguments: nap1, nap2 and nap3. The function writes to array nap3 the concatenation (joining) of the strings located in arrays nap1 and nap2. Assume that there is enough space in array nap3. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function rmLower that takes a char array as an argument and removes from it all characters that are lowercase letters. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function rmDigits that takes a char array as an argument and removes from it all characters that are digits. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function cutStr that takes as arguments a char array and two integers n and m, and cuts out from the received string the characters with indices from n to m (assuming that n<m). Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function wStrCopyNew that takes two arguments of type wchar_t[] (character arrays): a source and a destination. The function copies the string located in the source array into the destination array. Assume that there is enough space in the destination array. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function wStrConcat that takes three character arrays as arguments: nap1, nap2 and nap3 (use the wchar_t character type). The function writes to array nap3 the concatenation (joining) of the strings located in arrays nap1 and nap2. Assume that there is enough space in array nap3. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function w16 whose argument is a string. If the string contains characters other than digits, the function should return zero. If the string contains only digits, the function should return an integer formed by sequentially transcribing the digit characters. Assume that the string is exactly 3 characters long. In this task, do not use library functions other than input/output instructions. Create a test case. Use the wchar_t type in your solution.
Write a function rmOdd whose argument is a string. The function is supposed to remove characters from the string at odd indices. Create a test case.
Write a function copyEveryThird whose argument is a string. The function is supposed to return a new string that contains only every third character of the original string. Create a test case.

Example: For the string "ABCXYZ" the function should return "AX".

Write a function indexLower whose argument is a string. The function returns the index number at which the first lowercase letter from the left occurs. In the case of an empty string or no lowercase letters, the function should return zero. In this task, do not use library functions other than input/output instructions. Create a test case.
Write a function countOdds whose argument is a string. The function should return the number of odd digit characters appearing in the string. Create a test case.
Write a function toLowerNew that takes a pointer to a string of type const char* as an argument and returns a pointer to a new string in which all uppercase letters have been converted to lowercase. The original character array remains unchanged. Remember to allocate memory for the new string. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations and memory allocation functions. Create a test case for this function.
Write a function toUpperNew that takes a pointer to a string of type const char* as an argument and returns a pointer to a new string in which all lowercase letters have been converted to uppercase. The original character array remains unchanged. Remember to allocate memory for the new string. Do not use any built-in language functions other than input/output operations and memory allocation functions. Create a test case for this function.
